title: Recursive Coding Agents - Raymond Weitekamp, OpenProse
talk_summary: Raymond Weitekamp argues that agent reliability, not raw model intelligence, is the bottleneck, and that recursive language model (RLM) patterns—externalizing the prompt as a symbolic object, letting the model decide decomposition into sub-agent calls, and verifying sub-results in the parent—can be applied to coding agents. He demos wrapping an RLM as a tool, a fully recursive Pi agent, Claude Code dynamic workflows, and OpenProse, a markdown spec language that declares sub-agent work, verification, and tool/skill dependencies.

takeaways.technique: Parent-declared sub-agent decomposition with parent-side verification
takeaways.what_they_do: The parent agent decomposes a task into sub-agent calls, then verifies each sub-agent's returned work in the parent session rather than trusting it blindly; OpenProse makes this decomposition and verification explicit in a spec.
takeaways.evidence_quote: break a problem up into smaller pieces that are assigned to sub agents, verify the work of those sub agents um, in the in the parent agent session

takeaways.technique: Externalize large context and operate on it symbolically via a tool
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of reading a huge corpus into the context window, the agent gets an RLM-as-tool-call that explores the corpus symbolically and returns a distilled answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I just want to give my coding agent an RLM as a tool call ... we need to go sift through a 100 million token corpus
takeaways.numbers: RLMs process information many orders of magnitude larger than context window, tens of millions of tokens

takeaways.what_they_do: A coding agent harness calls an identical copy of itself to a configurable recursion depth, so sub-tasks get the same full toolset rather than a degraded sub-agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pi calls pi calls pi calls pi. You can set the depth however you want

takeaways.technique: Declare tool/skill dependencies per sub-agent role
takeaways.what_they_do: The workflow spec wires required skills and CLI tools as explicit dependencies so a sub-agent cannot run without the tools it needs for its role.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can add skills and tools as explicit dependencies ... or it can't run and do its job

takeaways.technique: Capture a golden session into a reusable workflow
takeaways.what_they_do: Take a successful agent session and have an agent deconstruct it into a reusable declarative workflow, so the good outcome can be reproduced repeatedly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take a golden session ... have the agent deconstruct that session and turn it into a reusable Prose workflow

takeaways.what_they_do: Run skeptical or red-team agents in parallel to adversarially probe the system, as an alternative to a single reviewer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: adversarial things such as having a skeptical agent or um you know, a red team uh set of agents
